**Needs changes before merge.** This is a SAFETY-tier review: the PR changes posted G-code of three posts.

### What is good

- The same-tool rule in the three posts agrees with `tormach.cps` (#1626). The first section always changes or names its tool, because `loadedTool` starts as `null`.
- `xyUnknown` stays `true` after a kept tool. The first traverse still comes after a Z-only rapid to the clearance (#1616). `each_traverse_states_its_height` pins this for all three posts.
- The kept-tool branch in TinyG writes no M5 / M9 again. The section end of the previous section already wrote them. G17 G90 and the WCS word are still written before the branch.
- Grbl 1.1 now counts `toolsLoaded` only for a real load. The first-load comment `LOAD T.. AND SET Z ZERO BEFORE THE START` stays correct.
- A setup change stops by default (`posting_setup_change.rs`, Pause / OptionalStop). That stop sets the tool to unknown, so a re-clamp also asks for the tool again.
- The decision record `docs/decisions/3445-grbl-same-tool.md` says why the Z lift and the spindle words stay.
- No recorded golden changed. This agrees with "Goldens moved: None".

### Results (trial merge with upstream/main `6e641dac7` merged at head `61daa2a2a`, locally)

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 58 steps, 0 failed (11.5 min).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Extra suites run:
  - `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test example_catalog`: 37 passed, 4 ignored.
  - `post suites: setup_change, script_grbl, script_grblhal, script_tinyg, grbl_dialect`: all pass.
  - `app suites: after_op, grblhal_post, tinyg_post`: all pass.
- Heavy lanes: `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main` on this head: 8 steps, 0 failed (release build plus `app heavy: conformance, control_comp, post_cycle_feed_spindle, probe_no_coolant, program_units, tinyg_post, wear_comp`).

### Mutations that I ran

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| `tinyg.cps` from upstream/main | red: the two `tinyg_*` tests |
| Grbl 1.1: `loadedTool = null` removed from the `stop` arm | red: `grbl_new_tool_return_and_stop_each_change_again` |
| All three posts: `loadedTool = null` removed from the `optional-stop` arm | **green**: all 6 tests, and the post and app suites above |

### Requested before merge

1. The optional-stop reset has no pinning test: `assets/posts/grblhal.cps:499`, `assets/posts/grbl.cps:503` and `assets/posts/tinyg.cps:531`. If this reset goes, the operator can change the tool at an `M1`. The next same-tool section then writes no `T M6` (no `M0` on Grbl 1.1), and the program cuts with a tool that the post did not ask for. This is a silent wrong program. Add an `optional-stop` case to each `*_new_tool_return_and_stop_each_change_again` test in `crates/post/tests/grbl_family_same_tool.rs`. For example: `post(s, m, &[(1, "optional-stop"), (1, "")])` gives `["T1 M6", "T1 M6"]` for grblHAL and TinyG, and on Grbl 1.1 one `TOOL CHANGE - LOAD T1` note with its `M0` after the `M1`. Then do the mutation again and name it in the body.

### Notes (not blocking)

- The `optionalStop` post option (the `M1` before a tool change) is now also not written for a kept tool. The body says this for grblHAL. This is correct: no tool change occurs.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Fixed the review finding on head `e97b5c5072fb04213bb6c7de879b4135a0fff1e1`.

### Changes

1. Optional-stop reset pin (`assets/posts/grblhal.cps:499`, `assets/posts/grbl.cps:503`, `assets/posts/tinyg.cps:531`):
   - Added an `optional-stop` (`M1`) case to each `*_new_tool_return_and_stop_each_change_again` test in `crates/post/tests/grbl_family_same_tool.rs`.
   - `grblhal_new_tool_return_and_stop_each_change_again` checks `post(s, m, &[(1, "optional-stop"), (1, "")])` writes one `M1` and `["T1 M6", "T1 M6"]`.
   - `grbl_new_tool_return_and_stop_each_change_again` checks one `M1`, one `TOOL CHANGE - LOAD T1` note, and one `M0` in that order (`M1` < `TOOL CHANGE - LOAD T1` < `M0`).
   - `tinyg_new_tool_return_and_stop_each_change_again` checks one `M1` and `["T1 M6", "T1 M6"]`.
   - Mutation check: removed `loadedTool = null;` from the `optional-stop` arm in all three posts. All three `*_new_tool_return_and_stop_each_change_again` tests failed (3 passed, 3 failed). Restored the three lines and all six tests passed.

### Verification on `e97b5c507`

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 58 steps, 0 failed.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: 8 steps, 0 failed.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test example_catalog`: 37 passed, 0 failed, 4 ignored.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Updated the PR body with the mutation result and final-head gate runs.

Ready for a re-review.

**Ready for the maintainer to merge.** This is a SAFETY-tier review: the PR changes the posted G-code of three posts (`grblhal.cps`, `grbl.cps`, `tinyg.cps`).

### Earlier finding (review of `61daa2a2a`)

1. The optional-stop reset had no pinning test. **Met.**
   - Commit `e97b5c507` adds an `optional-stop` case to each `*_new_tool_return_and_stop_each_change_again` test in `crates/post/tests/grbl_family_same_tool.rs`.
   - grblHAL and TinyG: one `M1`, then `["T1 M6", "T1 M6"]`.
   - Grbl 1.1: one `M1`, one `TOOL CHANGE - LOAD T1` note and one `M0`, in that order.
   - My mutations below make each of the three new cases red.

### What is good

- The same-tool rule agrees with `tormach.cps` (#1626). `loadedTool` starts as `null`, so the first section always changes or names its tool.
- A program stop and an optional stop set the tool to unknown in all three posts. The next section changes the tool again.
- `xyUnknown` stays `true` after a kept tool. The first traverse still comes after a Z-only rapid (#1616).
- The merge with upstream/main is clean. Main added the `arcFate` guard (#3442) to `onCircular` in the same three posts. That code is not near the tool-change code of this PR.
- The diff changes no recorded program. This agrees with "Goldens moved: None".
- The body has `Changelog:` and ends with `Fixes #3445`. The decision record `docs/decisions/3445-grbl-same-tool.md` is present. No process file, UI file, dependency or `testdata/` file changes.

### Results (trial merge of head `e97b5c507` with upstream/main `5346bd7ac`, locally)

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 60 steps, 0 failed (post: 38 steps, app: 22 steps).
- `cargo xtask gate light --base upstream/main`: 3 steps, 0 failed (release).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Extra suites run:
  - `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test example_catalog`: 37 passed, 0 failed, 4 ignored.
  - `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test example_catalog_adaptive --test example_catalog_edge_work`: 1 passed and 1 passed, 0 failed.
  - No `testdata/` or importer change: no kernel STEP suites are necessary.
- Heavy lanes: I did not run them again. The author's comment on this PR (2026-11-22T20:38Z) records `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main` on this head `e97b5c507`: 8 steps, 0 failed, against upstream/main `64b737729` (less than 1 hour old). The main changes since that base do not touch the tool-change code of this PR. The quick gate above ran the debug suites of the reached lanes (`conformance`, `tinyg_post`, `control_comp`, `program_units` and others) on the new trial merge. Upstream AGENTS.md ("Heavy lanes at review") asks no heavy step for a P3 PR.

### Mutations that I ran (on the trial merge)

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| `grblhal.cps`: `loadedTool = null` removed from the `stop` arm | red: `grblhal_new_tool_return_and_stop_each_change_again` |
| `grbl.cps`: `loadedTool = null` removed from the `optional-stop` arm | red: `grbl_new_tool_return_and_stop_each_change_again` (line 101, the new `M0` count) |
| `tinyg.cps`: `loadedTool = null` removed from the `optional-stop` arm | red: `tinyg_new_tool_return_and_stop_each_change_again` (line 131) |
| `tinyg.cps`: kept-tool branch off (`loadedTool === tNo` changed to `false`) | red: `tinyg_repeated_tool_writes_one_tool_change`, `tinyg_new_tool_return_and_stop_each_change_again` |
| All restored | green: 6 passed, 0 failed |

### Requested before merge

None.

### Notes (not blocking)

- The Z lift and the spindle stop and start between same-tool sections stay. The issue asks for them to go too. The decision record gives the reason. A follow-up issue can remove them if the maintainer wants that.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Second read (read-only, not built) of head e97b5c507. This comment has no review marker. I did not change a label.

Verdict: no blocker.

## The posted program at a section that keeps its tool
- Each of the three posts keeps: the line `G17 G90` with the work offset, the tool comment, the lift, and the rule that the first XY move waits for a Z move. grblHAL and Grbl 1.1 write `S M3` and the coolant again.
- Skipped: the tool call, the stop for the manual change (`M0`, the optional `M1`), and on TinyG the second lift.
- The stream sends the spindle speed for each section, and each section end writes `M5`. Thus each section starts its spindle again before a feed, also with a kept tool. A stream with no speed is refused, as before.
- The lift is not skipped. No XY move is at cutting depth.
- The comparison is by tool number. The app refuses two tools with one number.
- A stop (`M0`, `M1`) makes the tool unknown again, so the next section gets its full change.
- The first section always gets a full change: the loaded tool starts as `null`.

## Tests
Three sections with tool 1 give one tool change. A new tool, a return to an earlier tool, a stop and an optional stop each give a change again. The reviews confirm by mutation that the six tests are red on the old scripts. No golden changed, and that is correct: no recorded stream has two sections with one tool.

## Notes, not blockers (filed as https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/3565)
- The part of #3445 that this PR dropped on purpose (no `M5` and no lift between such sections).
- No pin for `S M3` before the first feed of a kept-tool section, and none for a different speed with the same tool.
- Mach3 (#2515) and Carvera.

## Not checked
I did not build. The trial merge with the current `main` runs here before the merge: the post crate, the app posting and conformance binaries, and the example catalog suites.
